rites.text: A practiced art that lets its users shape drifting haze and fumes into different effects. Those who master it can bend rising smoke to serve a range of purposes.

rites.name: Valasium Oreostaurum
rites.text: A bearer who is knocked down may instantly shift into a low, four-footed stance and stand again, spending one spark of fury to do so. Anyone already crouched on all fours gains nothing from it.

rites.name: Teleosanum Oriantausor
rites.text: A dim spectral art lets restless dead pierce a hidden membrane and watch the living from beyond. Unable to show themselves, they peer and spy, and the ground where it is practiced slowly breeds hollow voids.

rites.name: Valesia Virnestes
rites.text: A dormant state where a spirit sinks into its anchored keepsake for a long rest. Upon waking, the spirit mends a portion of its lost vitality.

rites.name: Valauntanum Amalanum
rites.text: A rare art that lets its masters bend chance so that lucky accidents tend to fall their way. It is never formally taught, yet it quietly passes from one practitioner to the next.

rites.name: Ciastus Amareonium
rites.text: A fighter lures an opponent toward a chosen target area, then abruptly folds into a smaller shape so the strike lands on empty air. The moment of vacancy opens a quicker counterattack.

rites.name: Lauliarnus
rites.text: A discipline that teaches its followers to resist torment and inner unrest only worsens the suffering. Adherents turn their anger and hatred into a tool, guiding it instead of letting it rule them.

rites.name: Reontus Niasium
rites.text: A discipline of practitioners who foresee coming happenings by counting patterns of decay and passing hours. They shape their craft through the forces that unravel matter and mark the flow of moments.

rites.name: Nisia
rites.text: A fighter in a non-beast shape lets an incoming blow land, then drops into a monstrous form and answers with a sharp counterattack that exploits the foe's openings.

rites.name: Coristum Coreosaunor
rites.text: A bound agreement of the sky-navigators that guides travelers by reading the heavens. It grants keen foresight and clear sight into hidden matters.

rites.name: Teleornoses
rites.text: A shaping that transforms a bearer's nature through a supernatural change. It is a term describing the altered form a being takes on.

rites.name: Amalontor
rites.text: A tense waking state in which a night-bound being weighs whether it may reach a sought-after peace. It marks the last stride before that peace is either granted or denied.

rites.name: Neosanum Teleontia
rites.text: A discipline practiced by a state bureau that reads minds and passes thoughts between people. It has three branches: sensing feelings, sharing thoughts, and reshaping them.

rites.name: Amilausanum
rites.text: A lineage of gamblers can sense the luck clinging to any person and siphon it away to bend events in their favor. Heavy use of this gift draws trouble and forces them to keep wandering.

rites.name: Ceosiarnia
rites.text: A miner's blessing lets a speaker spend a spark of enchantment to tap a short coded message onto a nearby surface. The knocks travel through solid material to a chosen listener, who understands them without effort.

rites.name: Renostus
rites.text: A strange inner power that certain altered folk gain once they pass through a transforming crisis. Each person who receives one wields it in a different way.

rites.name: Rallanum Teleolus
rites.text: A fighter whirls in place at great speed and lands a kick with crushing force. It resembles a spinning rear kick from a martial art.

rites.name: Nalium Coristus
rites.text: A craft that lets its practitioners reshape objects, keepsakes, and crafted relics by hand. Mastery begins only when the user accepts that every shaped material once held a living spirit.

rites.name: Losum
rites.text: A deliberate undoing of a strand within the world's woven fabric, used to bring back balance. It is performed by altering or destroying a portion of the pattern.

rites.name: Liantum Laneoranum
rites.text: A fighter rushes into a foe in a wolf-like shape, knocking their footing away, then shifts into a new form to exploit the fall. The surprise makes the second strike harder to defend against.

rites.name: Tornes Vanus
rites.text: These are the talents that various orders wield when they confront a spreading blight. Each order channels its own skill against the creeping sickness.

rites.name: Telarianus
rites.text: A rare blood sorcery practiced by night-dwelling hunters in distant lands, drawn from the faith traditions of enslaved folk. Its wielders are called sigil-weavers and must guard against spirits that seek to possess them.

rites.name: Tausteosia
rites.text: Beings of the unseen mind shape how one voice reaches another, bending the flow of speech and insight so that the listener learns what the speaker intends. Those who master it can make others trust false sights.

rites.name: Nastor
rites.text: A fighter rapidly reshapes the body so the part struck by an enemy is no longer there, then shifts into a new form to strike at any opening. It uses dodging skill and costs rage.

rites.name: Amaullum Orastus
rites.text: A practitioner's craft that moves a body across space in an instant by aligning distant points. Its name is slang for quick leaping.

rites.name: Tosteornor
rites.text: A practitioner seizes an opponent's wrist and twists it in the proper direction, pinning them without wrestling. Skill rather than brute force decides the hold.

rites.name: Teonaulia
rites.text: A battle-shape that a flesh-shaping blood clan takes on by reworking its own body. It is the form the clan adopts when preparing for war.

rites.name: Veostelium
rites.text: A hidden craft that lets a select blood-kin stir and sway the feelings of ordinary folk. Practitioners draw out and steer the passions of those around them.

rites.name: Drerath
rites.text: Drerath is a rite-event of the Holy Age in which the walled orders of Tasianium kindle a sacred flame across the high temples to seal the first crossing between the walled cities. The kindling tears open a brief rift of heat that scorches the stone of three sanctuaries before the wardens close it.

rites.name: Corenantus
rites.text: Hidden spirit-talents of the departed that may be taught or gained through hard experience. Stronger ones are harder to learn, yield greater power, and demand a steeper price to call upon.

rites.name: Neollauntus
rites.text: Every fractured being carries inner coping gifts that help them endure their broken nature. At the moment of breaking, each gains a steadfast resolve plus two further gifts shaped by their lineage.

rites.name: Teolanum
rites.text: A craft that lets its users move through a stormy, hazardous realm and carry willing companions along. When it fails, the user is flung into an unknown spot where dangers gather before they can get their bearings.

rites.name: Amasaurnes
rites.text: A practitioner's inner force that sets how firmly they can shape the world with their craft. Greater force makes failure less likely and allows more dazzling results when spells succeed.

rites.name: Vialanum
rites.text: A practitioner's presence becomes almost impossible for ordinary folk to notice or recall, and it can be lowered at will. Stronger versions can make the bearer's own name crumble and their form briefly slip out of the world.

rites.name: Millus Cauntor
rites.text: A undead-crafted practice that lets the bloodless drinkers of the night commune with restless wandering souls. No single lineage or brotherhood claims it, so any of them may study it, though at a steeper price to learn. It echoes several other arts of the same dark kind.

rites.name: Coresilles
rites.text: A learned craft lets a being draw life-sustaining essence from another's exhaled air rather than from their veins. It is open to anyone who finds the secret or a willing teacher, and it cannot be practiced by those of lowest potency.

rites.name: Ameosternor
rites.text: A undead being stirs its stored vital essence to briefly mimic a living body. It can then eat, feel warmth, and do things it once enjoyed, though the effect fades soon after.

rites.name: Voses
rites.text: A faint radiance seeps outward from every living, dead, and spiritual creature, showing what kind of being it is and how it currently feels.

rites.name: Nellia
rites.text: Undead blood-drinkers wield a craft drawn from their crimson life-essence, shaped by secret rituals and dark faiths. It stands as the most widespread and influential art among their kind.

rites.name: Veontum Amastor
rites.text: A dark mask-like shape taken on by a certain fallen lineage when they reveal their final form. It is one of several destructive forms open to members of their bloodline.

rites.name: Orollarium
rites.text: A blood-tied art by which a feeder spreads sickness selectively, bringing ailments upon the living or worsening those already brought low. Initiates are not truly accepted within their line until they have mastered it, and it works only on mortal flesh.

rites.name: Telontes
rites.text: A discipline of selective ruin that lets a practitioner unmake a chosen target while shifting the hidden variables of the world. It can dissolve resolve in a crisis, tilt disorder up or down, and quietly seeds the rebirth that follows collapse.

rites.name: Seraunia Liases
rites.text: A discipline that joins living flesh with engineered machinery through a practiced craft. Its practitioners shape the bond between organisms and mechanisms, drawing on the power of life itself.

rites.name: Raullesor
rites.text: A bearer of this gift slips effortlessly into any community, copying its gestures and speech as though born within it. The knowledge of that people's tongue fades once the gift runs its course.

rites.name: Nintum Valesianor
rites.text: A night-walker who sips only lightly from living prey, taking too little to end a life. The restraint is said to bring a calmer rest, since hunting less means sleeping more soundly.

rites.name: Taulles Tasanum
rites.text: A dark bond of loyalty forms when one person repeatedly drinks the life-blood of another, leaving the drinker bound to serve the giver. Some circles call it by other names.

rites.name: Maunastor
rites.text: A gifted practitioner reshapes their own flesh and form through inner will. Rarely can they impose such change onto another living being.

rites.name: Riarnanum
rites.text: A set of inherited talents that let the cursed outcasts slip into and adapt to the modern age. Their bearers are often said to carry a wild-hunter's blessing.

rites.name: Ciasanum Amaurnia
rites.text: Animals and people sense a hunter's hidden menace within a shapeshifter and flee from its presence. This dread makes ordinary bonds with others almost impossible, leaving only kin of the same nature as companions.

rites.name: Maurum
rites.text: A minor sealed art of the arcane that undoes another's enchantment as it forms. It needs only a single point of mastery to perform.

rites.name: Rirum
rites.text: A practitioner releases a spectral essence from their body to saturate a nearby region with lingering traces. Through these traces they sense distant surroundings and shape the environment in ways tied to a chosen attunement, working best where the setting matches that attunement.

rites.name: Laularus
rites.text: Each separate enchanted knack has its own distinct effect. Unlike deeper gifts, the means of working these knacks circulate widely among the fey folk, so no one kind of fey is tied closely to any particular knack.

rites.name: Rintor Sestanum
rites.text: A forbidden practice where one being devours another's essence to seize their power. It is perilous in an island realm, and a sleeping ancient horror is said to lie hidden beneath it.

rites.name: Maurnosanum
rites.text: A blended discipline that joins a sharpened sense of hearing with a limited shaping of the body. Practitioners combine these two arts into one technique.

rites.name: Orellium
rites.text: A protective inner mechanism that some sleepers' minds raise to shield themselves while they dream. It defends the dreamer against threats arising within their own sleeping mind.

rites.name: Taustia
rites.text: A jarring unraveling force that slowly weakens enchantments whenever it meets ordinary, unawakened folk. Practitioners of arcane arts find their workings fraying in such company.

rites.name: Amilum
rites.text: A hidden craft lets its practitioners rework the inner essence of another spirit from within. It is a discipline reserved for a particular guild of artisans who alter souls.

rites.name: Sintanum
rites.text: A discipline wielded by a powerful order that produces marvelous effects while operating inside its own rigid framework of belief. It is named by those who practice it to describe their achievements within that framework.

rites.name: Mestallia
rites.text: A joint discipline that blends mind-binding influence with bodily endurance. It is learned only once both foundational talents have reached their third tier.

rites.name: Veostor
rites.text: A practitioner's gift lets them perceive the flaws within an object and gauge how sound a living body is. A paired gift reveals the opposite, the vitality still flowing through things.

rites.name: Ameostes Soraulum
rites.text: A creature that devours another of its kind entirely, taking its essence and strength. The deed grows the consumer's power but corrupts its nature, leaving dark marks that others can see.

rites.name: Siarnia
rites.text: A specific gift tied directly to a bearer's core strength, letting them perform feats beyond ordinary limits. Most such gifts need little or no inner reserve to awaken, and one gift may be taken up more than once.

rites.name: Telaulia
rites.text: A secret craft of watching and recording that lets its users gather a great deal of knowledge from afar. A lesser use lets the practitioner wear another's face, though this usually costs the victim their life.

rites.name: Nillernia
rites.text: A variant of the distance-binding craft, first shaped by a reckoning guild and later mastered by a machine-minded order. It gradually spreads outward to allied circles and to lone practitioners who work through networked engines.

rites.name: Oronium
rites.text: A rare inner art practiced by an ancient order of embraced seers, letting them perceive how a chosen target fits into a vast mechanical design. They then reshape their own form to align with that design.

rites.name: Orilia
rites.text: A discipline of rational engineers who reach into a hidden inner realm and command the beings that dwell there. Its practitioners open passages into that unseen layer and bend the creatures and wandering spirits found within it.

rites.name: Telosanum
rites.text: A spirit-born discipline that lets a restless dead one master and quiet its inner hunger. It lets the bearer outmaneuver that hidden dark self and ignore its pull.

rites.name: Ameolor Corernallus
rites.text: A mental discipline that lets a practitioner shape glowing light and crackling current with the mind. It splits into three branches, covering currents, illumination, and machines.

rites.name: Lontiales
rites.text: A quick bodily reshaping that lets a wearer squirm free of crushing holds or tear loose from grasping claws. It must be used right after being struck, and a failed attempt can hurt the one trying it.

rites.name: Tiarnia
rites.text: A hereditary art by which a lineage of nobles drinks the vital essence of restless spirits. It works much like feeding on other undead, leaving the spirit drained.

rites.name: Corostasium
rites.text: A borrowed outer shape lets a mythic folk pass unnoticed among ordinary people. The shape shields them from a wearing-down force, and their character takes its form from it.

rites.name: Amausalus
rites.text: A common person is abruptly transformed into a gifted being when a dormant inner core awakens under extreme pressure. Raw cosmic force floods the body and quickly shapes itself into abilities that help the newly changed person survive a dire crisis.

rites.name: Tianes
rites.text: A short-lived disguise that a creature wears to pass as an ordinary attendant among mortals. It crumbles under close inspection or hard questioning, and is often forged through a brief bargain touching only minor matters of a person's life.

rites.name: Ciria
rites.text: A rare craft that lets its few practitioners plant thoughts or cravings into the minds of the living. Only a handful of users know its secrets, and it is quietly tied to two related arts.

rites.name: Teleolia
rites.text: A discipline of spectral fire that a bound, dead-touched people practice. Its corrupted variant is a ruinous blaze known as the scorched counterpart.

rites.name: Viastauria
rites.text: A ritual craft passed down among a recent lineage of proud rulers who study the patterns woven through a great urban center. Its practitioners can command a whole metropolis as though it were one living body.

rites.name: Veornus Taullores
rites.text: A ritual severs a caster permanently from their inner guiding spirit, ending their power to work magic and to be reborn. It comes in a partial form that trades spirit for relief from strain, and a total form that destroys the spirit entirely.

rites.name: Oraunium Tasiarus
rites.text: A ruling discipline over every natural and engineered energy in the material realm, from warmth and glow to currents and pulls. It cannot touch raw mystical power, yet lets its wielders hurl bolts of lightning, take flight, vanish from sight, or shake the ground.

rites.name: Sereostor
rites.text: A dark art that weaves convincing false scenes of a familiar living world to deceive a chosen spirit. Its illusions can distract the victim or slowly wear down their will, though casting it stirs the caster's own emotions and rarely do adepts learn it.

rites.name: Riles Valeniror
rites.text: A blunt, showy way of forcing raw energy through a hidden system so the result is loud and dramatic. It draws notice, so the user risks exposing themselves.

rites.name: Sereontasor
rites.text: A sudden, uncontrollable surge of instinct seizes those of the night, driving them toward fight or flight. It is a reflex that overrides reason whenever danger or hunger takes hold.

rites.name: Coroleornus
rites.text: A set of inner powers granted to certain blood-bound beings through their hidden twin. If their moral sense withers entirely, the twin devours their spirit and wears their face.

rites.name: Cales Mernollus
rites.text: A forbidden art that reshapes the form and behavior of ordinary matter in the living world. Its practitioners can twist objects into new structures and move them by will, and in later revisions they can also mend and forge spectral relics.

rites.name: Millerus
rites.text: A rare inner craft held by one lineage of night-bound feeders, letting them digest and draw strength from far more than ordinary folk could ever stomach. Their kin cheerfully earn the name of ravenous gorgers.

rites.name: Taurnontes
rites.text: A short-lived transformed shape that a hunter assumes, used only when bringing down prey. It is one of the bodily forms available to the wolf-blooded kin.

rites.name: Taurnes Seraulus
rites.text: A gifted spirit can command and animate lifeless objects, reshaping them or granting them new powers. Its practitioners are valued for turning the surrounding otherworldly material into useful tools, though misuse can trap or shatter the user.

rites.name: Masus Orintasus
rites.text: A wielder spends a spark of inner drive to tear a large nearby object loose and hammer it into a rough weapon in a single quick action. Only the wielder can use it without penalty; others struggle with it.

rites.name: Milia Vasanum
rites.text: A learned craft lets the undead draw sustenance from the wrongdoings of mortals rather than their blood. Any willing undead may study it, though only under a teacher from a particular order of ritual keepers.

rites.name: Vauntirnor
rites.text: A bound discipline lets a practitioner who studies carefully for several minutes and uses instruments uncover unseen forces. The insight gained reveals a foe's hidden vulnerabilities.

rites.name: Serilonor
rites.text: A codified guide that breaks down the workings of the arcane arts into their mechanics. It offers worked examples showing how practitioners can bring about specific kinds of wonders.

rites.name: Coresianus
rites.text: A shaped gift that silences machines within a short range. Any tool or device of chosen complexity stops working for a brief spell, leaving its parts intact but dormant.

rites.name: Mausellor
rites.text: A hidden art that turns a sleeping mind into a useful, dangerous tool. Its practitioners guard it closely and never teach it to outsiders, and most of its powers only work on those who are already asleep.

rites.name: Coraneolles
rites.text: A set of affinity talents that lets its wielders gather and shape knowledge. The most cunning fighters tend to learn it, and only spirits devoted to knowledge itself can pass it on.

rites.name: Coreornum Vaseolum
rites.text: A dark craft that exposes the flaws each blood-drinking kin carries within their lineage. Its strength grows with mastery, and it spares those whose lineage already bears the very weakness being forced upon them.

rites.name: Amelleostus
rites.text: A hidden shape that one of the fallen wardens may take, reserved for those of a particular lineage. It reshapes the bearer into a vast, terrifying visage tied to the land beneath.

rites.name: Mesintium
rites.text: A hushed craft through which a vampire siphons the feelings and fervor out of living people. The drinker gains lasting advantages from every stolen passion.

rites.name: Listesor
rites.text: A craft of shaping feeling through sound, letting its practitioners stir strong emotions in others through song, speech, or shouts. Its misuse can turn a gift into a torment for the one who wields it.

rites.name: Riantus Saurus
rites.text: A set of offensive and observing powers granted to chosen champions. Its practitioners are usually known as arbiters, though seekers of other paths may sometimes learn these gifts too.

rites.name: Vallorium
rites.text: A method by which a person sends their spirit outward, shaped more by their current frame of mind than by their core temperament. Those who have faced death repeatedly or carry a bold sense of purpose tend to manage it best.

rites.name: Coreolor
rites.text: A hidden craft that lets a practitioner keep a composed outward expression no matter what turmoil stirs within. It is passed down through one lineage of blood-drinkers and keeps their inner hunger from showing on their face.

rites.name: Neliantor
rites.text: A hidden art that stirs the hidden appetites of others, letting its wielder draw out indulgent desires and bind people with dazzling false visions. It belongs to a charming line of seducers who use it to gather like-minded companions.

rites.name: Canaurnium
rites.text: A practitioner who has pursued endless life through magic, either by drawing life from others or by preparing to outlast death as a spirit or wandering mind. Such pursuits are considered grim and often end violently.

rites.name: Oriarum Testanum
rites.text: A transforming mask-shape that a fallen spirit of one particular lineage can take on during its final, world-ending state. It reshapes the bearer into a terrible new appearance.

rites.name: Sentornor
rites.text: A practitioner entering a trance can draw up fragmentary glimpses of earlier and later existences, though only the pivotal moments surface. The gift fades entirely once the practitioner leaves their order.

rites.name: Oreosanum
rites.text: This is the reasoning, planning, social side that stays within a changed being after its transformation. Keeping it in balance with the wild urge is key, and fading away from it leaves the one turned to a hollow husk.

rites.name: Nintium Cantus
rites.text: A practitioner's inner faculty for perceiving hidden marvels and unseen forces around them. It does not always appear as sight and takes shape differently according to the discipline and the ruling force a seeker draws upon.

rites.name: Oriantor
rites.text: A craft for reading and steering the private hungers and tender obsessions of people. Its practitioners can inspire someone toward beauty or drive them into reckless indulgence, and the practice slowly bends the user toward their own darkest thoughts.

rites.name: Ceostanum Mellium
rites.text: A dark craft that pours a hungry void into living and dead alike, bending them into servants of a shared collective will. Its practitioners often preach it as a faith in the crowded streets of lawless cities.

rites.name: Rornasia
rites.text: This craft lets a hidden watcher observe a bound servant from afar and quietly steer their actions without being present. It works across great distances through unseen threads.

rites.name: Veolliaria
rites.text: A bloodline art that lets its wielders shape sound and singing into uncanny effects. It arose at the same time as a lineage of singers and remains bound to them.

rites.name: Vontaunes Vantestor
rites.text: A craft that lets its practitioners reshape living bodies by altering their inner chemistry and workings rather than merely their looks. It can work on others as well as oneself, and its strongest effects can reach ordinary people.

rites.name: Amistus Conantum
rites.text: A learned craft that lets seasoned wanderers of a dusky twilight realm slip between that hidden domain and the mortal world. Only those born with a natural gift for surviving its shadowed paths can wield it well.

rites.name: Teones
rites.text: A subtle craft that lets its wielders sway and speak with ordinary folk more persuasively, sharpening their social grace and, a little, their quiet movement and tongues. Any practitioner may learn it, regardless of their allegiance.

rites.name: Teliarum
rites.text: A craft by which a dark wanderer pushes fragments of its own being into places and creatures. Any of its kind can learn it, since imposing the self on others comes easily to them, and its workings carry a heavy, painful cost.

rites.name: Marnia
rites.text: A craft that lets a practitioner bend the flow of time, from nudging chance into fortunate coincidence to slowing or halting its passage. Its users also read the heavens to foresee coming events and reshape them.

rites.name: Sianeollium
rites.text: A discipline of the blood that lets its wielder conceal small objects, wear another's face, or vanish from sight entirely. It is practiced by those who prefer to remain unseen and to deceive.

rites.name: Sauliares
rites.text: A bearer attempts several deeds in a single moment, but each extra deed draws away a little of their focus. Those with swift reflexes may add deeds without losing any focus at all.

rites.name: Corisus Corintum
rites.text: A hidden art practiced by one serpentine line of undead that lets its users pierce the veil between worlds and draw a void-like emptiness into the material realm. Later rulebooks swapped it for a glassy necromantic path.

rites.name: Serausolium
rites.text: A shape some fallen beings take when they open passages between places. It belongs to one lineage of their kind and marks them as its heirs.

rites.name: Ciria Carnolles
rites.text: A fiery mask-form that a fallen spirit may take on in its final, world-ending guise. It belongs to one lineage of such beings and is shaped by the forging of their dark rites.

rites.name: Valiarniria
rites.text: A deceptive fighting method where a practitioner feigns clumsy stumbles and accidents to lure an opponent off guard. Then the practitioner strikes suddenly at a vulnerable spot from an unexpected angle.

rites.name: Lenaurium
rites.text: Open skills that any member of any clan or temperament can learn once they have earned enough accumulated honor. Hollowed outcasts automatically possess all of them but cannot learn or use any other abilities.

rites.name: Vollasus
rites.text: Individuals who wield a vast cosmic energy after a sudden shock, gaining a brain node that sets them apart from ordinary folk. Their gifts arise in a brief surge, shaped by the mind into forms it can grasp.

rites.name: Ameoriallum
rites.text: A practice of everyday effects that seem so ordinary to ordinary folk that they work without any strain of will. Such workings cannot stir backlash, and they form the shared agreement that holds the common world together.

rites.name: Lausia
rites.text: A practitioner can soften their own inner signature until watchers lose every trace of them. Those cloaked drift to the edges of ordinary life, and their deeds vanish from records and memory unless they stay out of the public eye.

rites.name: Coriantanum Marnes
rites.text: A set of hidden techniques that keep a being unnoticed and blend it into ordinary surroundings. They work by clouding meaning and by erasing or fixing what others remember.

rites.name: Orontelium
rites.text: A bodily technique in which a person shrinks to a smaller frame while held, letting them slip free of a grasp. Success adds to the escape effort, but a failed attempt causes extra harm and makes later escapes harder.

rites.name: Reolanum
rites.text: A method used by a guild that shapes what people believe is real by crafting moving images and other visual works. Its practitioners work mainly with the mind and with living things.

rites.name: Lornium Rallium
rites.text: A practitioner's visible halo of arcane force clings around their spirit. It reveals how skilled they are and how their personal path has shaped them.

rites.name: Orarnia Vaunilum
rites.text: A branch of study that sits within a larger mental discipline, one of three distinct fields focused on a single kind of inner power. It separates the shifting of solid things from the stirring and calming of tiny particles.

rites.name: Viallanum Causes
rites.text: A ravenous craving that seizes a creature whose inner gifts have been drawn heavily upon. It drives the sufferer to seek out a life-sustaining essence to restore their strength.

rites.name: Oreosirnium Meniastus
rites.text: An umbrella term for the supernatural gifts that ordinary folk may hold in this world. Its most common forms are mind-powers, spellcraft, and devout miracles, and the same gift may rest in a human or a non-human being alike.

rites.name: Oreontor Tistus
rites.text: A gift granted to seers that lets one reader tell fortunes once per span of days, using any divining tool chosen. It works like an innate sense of practical judgment, though the gifted may also acquire that sense through training.

rites.name: Mirnus
rites.text: A newly devised discipline of inner growth taught by a cursed, weakened brood of night-drinkers. It arose only after a great holy war against the undead began.

rites.name: Roriantanum
rites.text: A rare craft belonging to one lineage of blood-drinkers that sharpens their hunger. It lets them draw the life-essence of their own kind more readily than others could.

rites.name: Seriles Orontiles
rites.text: A practitioner's private bond to a distant lookout, drawing a steady flow of power that lets them shape the world. It also tints how they perceive hidden forces, forever.

rites.name: Nistes
rites.text: A discipline of bending unseen energies, practiced by a secretive guild of adepts. It is split into three paths: channeling raw force, reinforcing the body, and reshaping matter.

rites.name: Serauntium Noneoles
rites.text: A synthetic mind-user is grown in one of eight sealed vats that wake a dormant latent to inner awareness. Each vat locks the awakened person into a single mental discipline.

rites.name: Serilor
rites.text: A discipline that teaches its wielders how ancient stone and peaks can hold corrosive substances that wear away living things. A purer variant of the same practice is also known.

rites.name: Orintia Telentium
rites.text: A gift granted to a gifted seer-kind that sharpens one chosen sense, lending a bonus to noticing things through it. The bearer may briefly pour a spark of inner power into that sense to perceive feats far beyond ordinary reach.

rites.name: Meonoles
rites.text: A moral code that undead drinkers of blood follow to hold back their hunger. Adherents adopt its discipline as a way to resist the savage urge within them.

rites.name: Valeorenor
rites.text: A person who gains strength by siphoning the inner life force of other living creatures through a mental talent. The talent may be born within them or acquired from an outside source.

rites.name: Rirum Neollanum
rites.text: A swift-handed craft that sharpens a practitioner's nimbleness, growing from a dark tie between a rare blood-line and a shadowed, beast-like presence.

rites.name: Vallausium
rites.text: A learned pattern describing how a creature of the night prefers to take sustenance, and when. It is a tendency rather than a rule, and it grants certain bonuses in skills, talents, and powers, along with gifts and burdens.

rites.name: Valiarum
rites.text: A hidden art that breeds quarrels and distrust among humans, ghouls, and undead alike, leaving ruined bonds behind. Shunned by many, it is quietly hired by powerful undead to weaken their rivals.

rites.name: Seriantium Niastium
rites.text: A hidden mental art that blends mind-reading with inner healing, reaching out to those whose hearts run warm yet who are drawn to the strange. It grants great insight but risks turning its users into wild hunters of their own kind.

rites.name: Colleornium
rites.text: A mind-born craft that lets adepts bend matter through will, chilling or heating the air, sensing the hidden shape of objects, and nudging small weights a few fingers' width at a time.

rites.name: Corernes
rites.text: These inborn changes let certain dark beings move in unusual, specialized ways. Each alteration gives a creature a distinct method of travel.

rites.name: Lileoranum
rites.text: A steady inner hum rising from an awakened person's longings against the dull world around them. It shapes how their sorcery unfolds and makes them feel strange and potent to ordinary folk.

rites.name: Viareolor
rites.text: A tormented brood of night-walkers can bend the shadowed dreamland their own fears create. They open its hollow passages as a road between places, or push their nightmare onto unwilling victims.

rites.name: Telonium Oraseolanum
rites.text: A mortal who glimpses a cast-down being in its true radiant shape either falls into awe or is seized by terror, and the being can siphon a little of his inner conviction from him.

rites.name: Oriarium Reosum
rites.text: A set of spirit-calling practices that let a hunter borrow powers from unpredictable spirits by first appeasing them with thanks, offerings, or sacrifices. Its knowledge is guarded closely and passed only after long searches for a willing teacher.

rites.name: Lausiantia
rites.text: A learned capacity that a person gains through practice and training. It is paired with a natural talent to build a pool of dice for any deliberate action.

rites.name: Amistum
rites.text: A shapeshifting people speak through pulses of electric current that travel between them. The practice is a communication method unique to their kind.

rites.name: Lilanum Orianes
rites.text: A set of sorcerous bindings used by the most estranged of a mirrored people, who slip their hold on the world and bend its laws to their will.

rites.name: Leliarnanum
rites.text: A bond where one undead being makes another of its kind, and the newly made one is known as the maker's ward. The maker stands as the origin of that new being's existence.

rites.name: Callor Valaunes
rites.text: A rare gift lets a seer sense the awakening of hidden chosen ones before they understand their own nature. The sensed will then be guided toward their destiny.

rites.name: Lolanum Tiarium
rites.text: A trained sense lets certain watchers tell unnatural presences from ordinary folk. It reveals that something is wrong, but not what the thing truly is, and it pierces false images and illusions.

rites.name: Valentium
rites.text: A set of gifts given to chosen wanderers by spirits dwelling in engines and currents. These gifts let its bearers command clever devices and turn them to great advantage, and it is favored most by a guild of metal-wielding craftsfolk, though wanderers of other kinds in crowded cities find it useful too.

rites.name: Mornistum
rites.text: A innate resilience lets otherworldly beings withstand magical powers, whether their own kind or foreign. It shields them against workings aimed at their very nature.

rites.name: Amillaunes
rites.text: A mind-based power that lets a user move objects, handle fine tasks at a distance, and raise invisible barriers against fast strikes. Variations can thunder the air, reshape air pressure, or choreograph motion into objects.

rites.name: Riantum Rialanum
rites.text: A bloodline of undead wanderers keeps a lingering pull toward the night sky's pale orb, expressed as a craft of moonward instinct. Its gifts are muted when used among only their own kind.

rites.name: Miasternium
rites.text: A craft that only the weak-blooded can practice, reshaping the vital fluid within living bodies. It has become the most widely followed art of modern blood-working.

rites.name: Valistia Coraustor
rites.text: A spectral mark that a ghostly being can summon to twist its shape into a grim reflection of its own inner nature. Using it swiftly stirs up a sour, lingering ill will.

rites.name: Colanum Telausanum
rites.text: Practitioners fuse two distinct disciplines into a single hybrid art. It demands a mastered foundation, a second discipline studied to a set depth, and long stretches of trial and steady inner investment, yet it yields abilities few others can match.

rites.name: Tillanum Rellanum
rites.text: A recognized discipline of arcane practice that lets awakened practitioners draw otherworldly presences into their working. Learned scholars study it as one of the established channels of the craft.

rites.name: Tistum Siallausium
rites.text: This power governs distance, dimension, and scale, letting a skilled user step instantly between places through openings, look across great gaps, raise barriers against unseen eyes, and bind links between objects and beings.

rites.name: Merniasia
rites.text: A discipline in which trained minds bend the distance between places, shifting either their own bodies or objects to new locations. Practitioners sense the shapes and positions of nearby things, which lets them notice incoming travelers and trace where recent movements occurred.

rites.name: Ronus Amausalor
rites.text: A set of celestial gifts granted to a single lunar-aligned bearer. Each gift succeeds automatically once invoked and may only be called upon one time per encounter.

rites.name: Teleornes Cornerum
rites.text: A force of order and preservation that holds the world steady and is bound to reason, machines, and speech. It is one of three opposed forces that together shape how reality behaves.

rites.name: Resostum
rites.text: A bound chant that tears apart a made thing when it is sung. It is recorded in a single long tale kept by wandering storytellers.

rites.name: Tentaulia
rites.text: A dark craft by which spectral wanderers bend a churning storm-realm to their will, carving hollow pockets for travel. It also opens lasting trails through a maze of shadow, many first cut by fallen fiends.

rites.name: Telilonium
rites.text: A ritual lets a seeker commune with the beast hidden inside them, unlocking hidden strength drawn from their darker nature. Once learned, the practice cannot be unlearned, even after the seeker abandons their order.

rites.name: Amarnausor
rites.text: A discipline that lets certain beings bend and command machinery and engineered devices. It works in a manner akin to a mechanical sorcery drawn from an alternate age of gloom.

rites.name: Lausum Orisia
rites.text: A mental discipline practiced by a secretive ruling method that reshapes a person's beliefs. It works by quietly altering how an individual thinks about the world.

rites.name: Costeorum
rites.text: A discipline that divides a being's inner self into two opposing halves, granting sharper restraint at the cost of letting the savage half surface now and then. Its practitioners are feared as unstable, split-minded figures.

rites.name: Terium
rites.text: A practiced art by which a trained wielder draws on unseen layers of existence to reshape what can be perceived, or to glimpse what ordinary sight conceals.

rites.name: Mollirnor
rites.text: A dark craft that lets wandering ghosts ride the furious winds of a storm and bend those winds slightly to their will. Scouts who reach a ruined city ahead of the main host often practice it, and cruel phantoms use it to harass other travelers caught in the gusts.

rites.name: Siarnum Valostum
rites.text: A tracing craft lets its practitioners slip into normally hidden streams of watchful data, like camera feeds and location beacons. Each mastered thread opens a separate channel, but careless use draws the notice of those who keep the peace.

rites.name: Telaustor
rites.text: A foul wave of city stenches is loosed to overwhelm a target's nose. Sharp-scented foes are dazed, and a berserk ally can be jolted free of their frenzy.

rites.name: Corinia
rites.text: A rare inner power is held by a fringe lineage of deformed blood-drinkers. They twist their bodies further into grotesque forms that draw in and repulse whoever watches.

rites.name: Amiantollia
rites.text: A bound one who shatters a spirit's anchor to break its will, seizing its power without any duty owed to the departed. Such binders gather in crews and often clash with those who honor the dead.

rites.name: Telaselor
rites.text: A bloodborne power that lets its wielders surpass ordinary strength by many times. Its feats can warp surroundings and shatter bodies, making duels with it grim and perilous to witness.

rites.name: Amenasanum
rites.text: A borrowed everyday identity that the long-lived wear as a cover, letting them pass unnoticed among ordinary people whose ears would not recognize their true titles.

rites.name: Tauntes Renor
rites.text: A rare gift lets certain gifted seers perceive the wider pattern of things. They read the weaknesses of foes, glimpse what came before, and guide allies toward better futures.

rites.name: Oreolia Veostarnium
rites.text: A tactic by which a shadowy watching order reshapes the threads that bind a community together. It lets its wielders tilt those ties toward outcomes that favor their own circle and allegiance.

rites.name: Viasus Tianium
rites.text: A reshaping art in which a made being's core substance is altered into something stronger, unlocking extraordinary abilities. It is practiced by beings born of a crafted origin.

rites.name: Serausor Vaurnanum
rites.text: A flagrant working of willpower that visibly bends the world beyond what onlookers accept as possible, so reality pushes back against it. Whether it counts depends on the expectations of the local community.

rites.name: Coriarus Relles
rites.text: Fleeting afflictions that take hold of fighters during clashes, unlike lasting ailments. They come as personal strains that a single fighter can shake off, or as area strains that spread over everyone nearby and can only be eased for an entire encounter.

rites.name: Lentarnium
rites.text: A caster inscribes a sealed name onto a clay token, grinds it into dust, and feeds it to a small animal. Through the creature's body, the caster can speak to and hear the named distant person.

rites.name: Rollastus
rites.text: A servant of the hidden folk may spend a spark of inner strength to finish a modest chore in a fraction of its usual time, provided no onlooker sees the work. Such a helper also slips past notice more easily.

rites.name: Valia Teloleontum
rites.text: Each chosen seeker holds to a guiding conviction that shapes how they confront dreadful beings. Devotion deepens their power, yet those who surrender wholly to it often fall into madness.

rites.name: Valostor Verum
rites.text: A ruling discipline lets a practitioner glimpse outcomes beyond the present and bend the flow of moments around themselves or others. Its skilled users can peer into bygone days and forthcoming ones, and sometimes move things across the ages.

rites.name: Caustor Lireolum
rites.text: A set of gifts shared by metalworkers and outcasts living within crowded city streets. Spirits of scavenging creatures that have learned to thrive among people can pass these gifts on to those who seek them.

rites.name: Tentor Valliarium
rites.text: A guide that describes many forms of folk sorcery practiced in a shadowed modern-era world. These informal workings are commonly called hedge magic by the people who use them.

rites.name: Lirnanum
rites.text: Lirnanum is a sect of silent bone-wardens in the sunken cathedrals of Tasianium, who bind their marrow-song into a single tide so that many bodies fuse into one vast, shifting weapon. Their discipline is taught in cycles of mirrored breath, where a novice learns to hear the pulse of every fellow warden and then surrender her own. When the old oaths are sung in full, the sect can still drown a fortress of stone in the tide they raise.

rites.name: Cenolia
rites.text: Cenolia is the resonant mother-tone of the Tasianium chorus, a presence felt as a hum in deep stone rather than a body seen in light. She is said to have taught the first mourners to sing the dead into the earth, and her echo still shapes how the realm mourns and remembers.

rites.name: Saunores
rites.text: Saunores is a mournful lineage of grave-keepers in Tasianium, whose members speak with the departed through hollowed ash and salted bone. In the third age they were quietly absorbed into a larger house of spirit-wardens, and their old rites now survive only as inherited habits of silence.

rites.name: Orolium
rites.text: Orolium is a dwindling lineage born of pale night-stalkers who mated with the hollow-eyed folk of the thorn-marches, passing down a gift for bending dusk and fey glamour. Each generation sheds a little more of its humanity, so the eldest of them wear smiles that no mortal face could hold.

rites.name: Amistium
rites.text: Amistium is a concept of ritual inheritance in Tasianium's mythic age, a lineage of hollow-eyed mourners who keep the dead's last heat alive by drawing it into their own marrow. Their rites stored grief as fuel, letting a single bell-toll carry the force of a shattered hill. Their name survives only in the ledgers of the Veyra conclave, which folded their practice into its own.

rites.name: Oriallor
rites.text: Oriallor is a loose tradition of grave-keepers in the Tasianium mythic era, whose practitioners slowly rot in visible patches as they draw on the dying energies they gather. Their rites are said to unmake bonds of breath and memory, and the scene of their work is felt across entire valleys before the crops fail.

rites.name: Valiantia
rites.text: Valiantia is a vanished lineage of oath-bound duelists in the Tasianium myths, whose blood lets them perceive and bend the flow of moments rather than surrender to fury. Their last recorded stand came at a sunken bell-tower where a single hour was stretched into a long winter. Few scholars now believe the tales are more than fond exaggerations.

rites.name: Rorniastes
rites.text: Rorniastes is a concept of a lineage of women in the Tasianium cosmos who wear their deaths like veils, shedding skin and bone to become coiled, sibilant shapes that drink the last breath from the dying. Their power is tied to the boundary between a living body and the silence beyond it, a rite of passage marked by the molting of their former selves.

rites.name: Seontus
rites.text: A spirit's wandering trace through a hidden otherworld, shaped by the traveler's perception. Some routes are reliable bridges while others vanish mid-passage, and a few strange conveyances and flying paths also exist there.

rites.name: Liarnum
rites.text: A family of inner-mind powers that each group of practitioners specializes in. Every such family holds three modes, each a distinct mental ability.

rites.name: Amenialium
rites.text: Gifted minds sense the hidden energy in living bodies and reshape organic matter into tools. Ordinary people who attempt advanced crafts are drained or driven to ruin.

rites.name: Amolus
rites.text: A flexible art of reshaping the deepest rules of existence through an awakened mind's resolve. Its users draw many distinct effects from shared foundations, and their workings can provoke a dangerous rebound.

rites.name: Rilor Raureosus
rites.text: A class of inner powers held by a devouring kind, paralleling the ancestral gifts of another kind. They cannot be used by the devourers unless first taken from another, and each use costs a store of spent hunger.

rites.name: Talistus
rites.text: A dark craft that keeps a restless dead host linked in constant contact, letting them share thought as one swarming intelligence. Only the most practiced can pull knowledge and messages from the shared current.

rites.name: Sauntus Veranum
rites.text: A dark craft by which restless dead drain the void around them to feed their hollow forms. Practicing it courts peril, since meddling with the void invites rivals who resent the competition, and it can also stir the scattered remnants of the self back toward life.

rites.name: Teornes Teleosor
rites.text: Hidden arts of the cosmos, these evocations hold the foundations of reality and steer its forces. Fallen beings regain them slowly as their vessels grow attuned to celestial power.

rites.name: Nalaunus
rites.text: A craft by which certain beings bend the arrangement of space itself. It made room for matter to exist and lets its wielders link distant places however they choose.

rites.name: Corirnostus
rites.text: Certain quantum-touched wielders have their innate traits boosted past human limits, granting feats like great strength, striking allure, and swift mastery of knowledge. Some also gain sharpened extra talents, such as leaping high or reshaping their own features.

rites.name: Ventanum Oriallia
rites.text: A subtle craft that links the thoughts of every reasoning creature through a shared deep current. It pairs with a twin discipline of space and governs a realm of unbridled dreams and whispers.

rites.name: Milleoria
rites.text: A bundle of mystical abilities shared among divine beings and their descendants, grouped by theme. Each individual ability within the bundle can be learned, though some require special means or a sacred token.

rites.name: Vaunus Orialeorum
rites.text: A foundational craft that governs the raw essence of sorcery itself. Practitioners reshape the bare energy beneath all enchantment, mending others' workings and granting ordinary objects strange power.

rites.name: Tones Orollum
rites.text: A cosmic force that reshapes a vessel piece by piece while driving change through the cycle of breaking and building anew. It channels growth born from ruin and continual renewal.

rites.name: Millianus
rites.text: A mental discipline that lets a practitioner reshape their own body, grow spare organs, and dissolve the molecular bonds holding a foe together. Some of its arts can also be turned outward to alter others.

rites.name: Cillus
rites.text: A shorthand term for the energy that gifted users can reach and reshape through a hidden inner gate. Its users shape the four basic natural forces, so their reach is set only by their own mind.

rites.name: Volor Telirausor
rites.text: A mighty binding power that lets an ancient elder bend a chosen art toward whatever purpose the elder requires. Its uses range from mass mental control to swarms of vermin, shadowed clouds, and fusion with the land.

rites.name: Lanisium
rites.text: A departing spirit slowly releases its lingering attachments through a ritual of farewell. As each bond weakens to nothing, the spirit gains freedom to wander the afterlands and moves closer to ascension.

rites.name: Amistares
rites.text: A method of projection that lets a practitioner glide between the living world and the realm of the dead. It is more adaptable than other projection methods, crossing the boundary with greater ease.

rites.name: Salium Seorus
rites.text: A rare inner craft that lets its practitioner bend the passage of moments around them. It is said to be a sharpened form of swift movement, reaching into the very flow of time.

rites.name: Sintiastor
rites.text: A final hidden power that would let a seeker transcend their limits once every pattern is fulfilled. Long dismissed as a rumor, it is now sensed through a crimson beacon in the sky.

rites.name: Nostelum
rites.text: A divine fragment is fitted into a mortal frame, granting powers beyond ordinary limits. Its celestial keeper clears away the memories of a past life and prepares the bearer for a new one.

rites.name: Telarnor Lirus
rites.text: A far-reaching sensing technique devised by a cosmic guild of void-workers. It lets practitioners perceive distant bodies across great interstellar gulfs, though it grows blunt when examining things that lie close at hand.

rites.name: Volus Caurollia
rites.text: A practitioner folds the air around them to leap across distance, vanishing from one place and appearing in another. Some can also split into two linked forms, though each is weaker than the whole.

rites.name: Valoreostes
rites.text: A mind-born craft lets a practitioner move objects and beings across space by instant transfer. Greater mastery carries living travelers across great distances and can even split a thing into pieces.

rites.name: Oreosentor
rites.text: A mystical state that the oldest beings of the fae might reach once they gather enough accumulated honors. It lifts them beyond the ancient gods, though none can say what waits beyond that threshold.
